clock.source: timing table row 7680ms, verified to close

choreography_model: parallel zone loops on one clock, not a linear storyboard
storyboard_reconciliation: The brief describes six sequential scenes over 8-10s. Six sequential node states alone need 5.4s at a readable 900ms dwell, which would leave no time for the rest, and a scene-by-scene build would leave frame 0 mostly empty and fail the first-frame gate. Every scene is therefore kept but run as a concurrent zone pass on the shared clock, so the whole composition is present at every instant and motion carries state rather than construction.

tracks.mechanic: Both tokens leave SIGNAL together at 50% of the loop. The AI-assisted token stops once at INTERPRETATION and reaches DECISION at 72%. The manual token dwells at COLLECT, COMPARE, INTERPRET and SUMMARISE and does not reach DECISION until 30% of the following loop. The gap is the argument, and it is deliberately wider than one cycle: the slow route does not fit in the time the fast route finishes in.
tracks.implementation: SMIL animateMotion, keyTimes/keyPoints with dwell windows, rotate=0, shared -0.5 loop phase so the seam falls mid-loop

measured_windows.seam: mid-loop, hidden by the token fade
measured_windows.note: SMIL local cycle is offset half a loop by begin=-3.84s, so local and loop percentages differ by 50.

tracks.mechanic: One token per wire travels from its platform chip to the interpretation panel. Token colour matches the signal class the wire encodes. Six wires, staggered 6% apart, directional not bouncing.
tracks.implementation: SMIL animateMotion with mpath referencing the wire path itself, so each route geometry exists once. CSS carries only the opacity fade that hides the reset.

tracks.mechanic: The assistant releases its insight card down into the example-output block, then a marker steps through the three lines in order.
tracks.implementation: CSS transform + a stepped top marker

tracks.mechanic: A cobalt evidence outline touches TEST, then WAIT, then MOVE BUDGET, one at a time and never overlapping. The cursor then leaves the buyer's raised hand, travels to MOVE BUDGET, and the green selected state plus check badge holds to the end of the loop.
tracks.implementation: stepped border-color per chip. Delays shift a clock FORWARD, so the later chip uses -0.92 loop, not -0.08. With steps(1,end) the value holds from the keyframe it is declared on, so each window opens at its own keyframe percentage.
tracks.message_constraint: The cursor originates at the human mascot. The AI mascot has no track that reaches a decision chip. This is the one motion rule that may not be relaxed for pacing.

measured_windows.method: probed from the captured frames at build/.frames, not asserted from the keyframe source

tracks.mechanic: Six nodes light one at a time for 1280ms each, filling the whole loop. Reverse-ordered negative delays so the order is 01 to 06 and node 01 is already lit on frame 0.
From 54% the five middle stages of the manual chain fade to 20% and scale to 0.84, so the chain visibly compresses. At 72% the DECISION pill on the assisted row fills solid green. Restored by 98%.
tracks.implementation: opacity plus scale transform, which does not reflow the flex row

tracks.mechanic: The AI assistant floats 3px on a four-phase cycle. The buyer stays still: the character who makes the decision does not fidget.

frame_zero_contract: Every zone that carries meaning resolves at t=0: the manual chain is complete and undimmed, node 01 is lit, MOVE BUDGET is selected with its check badge, and the two rail tokens sit at opposite ends of their routes with the gap open. Travelling elements are the deliberate exception: the nine signal tokens and the cursor are held at opacity 0 at their seam, because a token frozen mid-wire in a screenshot reads as a rendering artefact. The rule is that frame 0 must be a complete infographic, not that every element must be visible in it.

budget_plan.ground: light with a 54px grid, so motion must stay tight and local

seekability: CSS keyframes and SMIL only. No requestAnimationFrame, no transitions, no canvas, no runtime library.
verification: Decision order and node order are both probed from captured frames rather than read off the source. Two source-level traps were found this way and fixed: a negative delay that inverted TEST and WAIT, and an animation shorthand on .dec.sel that replaced the evidence keyframes so MOVE BUDGET never showed its pass.
